transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE on this account, with Priya and Ethan from SE. How's everyone?
[00:08] Dr. Laura Martinez (Cascade): Hi Alex, thanks. Laura here. We're excited to scope this pilot; security is the big thing for us.
[00:14] Mark Rivers (Cascade): Mark, cloud eng. We'll be hands-on for benchmarks and infra questions.
[00:18] Priya Patel (Redwood): Great, quick agenda from our side — cover success criteria, estimate workload, propose bench plan, then deep dive into security requirements.
[00:27] Sophie Tan (Cascade): Sounds good.
[00:29] Kevin O'Neil (Cascade): Kevin, security. I'll lead the compliance bits.
[00:32] Alex: Perfect. So first, success criteria — Laura, what would success look like for Cascade at end of pilot?
[00:41] Laura: For us it's twofold. One, functional correctness — model responses must meet our quality bar on the triage assistant use case. Two, security compliance — no PHI leakage, auditability, and ability to run under our VPC. If both are green, we'll move to a 3-month dedicated contract.
[01:03] Priya: Good — can you quantify the quality bar? e.g., NDCG, pass rate on a test set?
[01:09] Sophie: We have a labeled set of 500 triage prompts with expected outcomes. KPI is 85% alignment on key intent labels and sub-entity extraction recall above 90%.
[01:19] Alex: Great, we'll use that as the eval set during bench.
[01:22] Mark: On throughput — current expectation is roughly 10k requests per day, peak 120 RPS for short bursts, average concurrency around 8. Payloads are ~1.2k tokens on avg, sometimes up to 3k.
[01:36] Priya: Thanks, that's super helpful. For benching we should capture latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. Also memory/KV cache hit rates.
[01:47] Ethan: Quick note — we have automatic KV caching and prefix caching. We'll instrument cache hits during bench. Sometimes transcripts show 'KV cash' in our notes, ha, it's 'KV cache'.
[01:55] (laughter)
[02:00] Alex: Ok security — Kevin, what corporate requirements must Redwood meet for the pilot?
[02:07] Kevin: SOC 2 Type II is baseline. ISO 27001 preferred. We need SSO via SAML with Just-In-Time provisioning, RBAC mappings so our admins can control who can call the model, audit logs retained 365 days, and KMS integration or bring-your-own-key for secrets. Also data residency: any customer data must stay in us-west-2 for now.
[02:34] Priya: We're SOC2 and ISO27k compliant; we'll attach certificates. We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with fine-grained API key scoping. Audit logs can be streamed to customer SIEM via syslog or S3 export. KMS: we support a few KMS integrations and have options for BYOK/HSM in private deployments.
[02:58] Kevin: Good. For the hosted POC we want to validate that logs show request-level metadata including token counts and user id mapping, and that keys are rotated and never exposed.
[03:10] Priya: We can include an audit artifact in the bench report. For hosted we can restrict via IP allowlist and customer-specific routing to us-west-2. For more isolation we can propose a Dedicated pool or Private VPC for the pilot.
[03:24] Mark: Dedicated sounds preferable if we need guaranteed throughput. But our security team prefers a VPC option even for pilot. What's the timeline to stand up a Private deployment?
[03:34] Alex: Private is more involved. Bare minimum 2-3 weeks for a simple VPC deploy with our private control plane, assuming we have networking info and KMS access. Dedicated pools can be faster if we're talking reserved capacity in us-west-2, like 5-7 business days for allocation.
[03:50] Laura: Timeline-wise, we'd like pilot bench results within 4 weeks and a go/no-go decision by week 6. Is that realistic?
[03:58] Priya: Yes. Proposed cadence: Week 0 (now) exchange security docs and sample data; Week 1-2 setup SSO + test infra; Week 2 run bench; Week 3 analyze results and iterate; Week 4 decision and contract talk by week 6.
[04:14] Kevin: Sounds fine. On SSO — we use Okta, will need SAML metadata and SCIM for user sync. We want to map our Azure AD groups to Redwood roles.
[04:24] Alex: Okta + SCIM supported. We'll send SAML metadata and a SCIM endpoint for test sandbox. We'll need an admin liaison.
[04:31] Sophie: We'll be the liaison — Sophie.
[04:33] (00:04:35) Mark: About benchmarks — what exact metrics will you capture?
[04:38] Priya: Latency p50/p95/p99, end-to-end request time, tokens/sec, throughput (requests/sec), cost estimates, KV cache hit rate, and model quality on your 500-sample eval set. We'll also collect system metrics: GPU util, memory, disk I/O for Private.
[04:52] Mark: For tokens — our average payloads 1.2k tokens, but the model may generate 200-400 tokens back. We'll include that in the bench.
[04:59] Alex: On data handling, can you confirm whether you'll provide PHI in the sample set or redacted data?
[05:05] Laura: We'll provide redacted samples for bench; if we move to Dedicated/Private we may run with live PHI under BAAs. For the pilot we want to validate that logs never store raw input anywhere accessible.
[05:17] Priya: Understood. For hosted, we support configurable retention and can disable certain logging fields. For dedicated/private, customer controls more. We'll document exact fields in the workbook.
[05:28] Kevin: Audit logs: we need immutable logs with user/action/request id, and ability to export to our SIEM nightly. Retention 365 days. Also need proof of regular key rotation and access control for keys.
[05:40] Ethan: We can stream to S3 with server-side encryption and an option to push to your SIEM. Key rotation is supported and we can provide rotation logs.
[05:47] (lipsmacking)
[05:50] Sophie: A few operational Qs — what's the expected cost during bench? We want an estimate to include in our internal budget.
[05:57] Alex: We'll provide ballpark cost per 1k tokens and an estimated monthly run rate based on the 10k/day estimate. Priya will include bench-run cost and an optimized configuration (quantization / batching) to reduce unit cost.
[06:10] Mark: Any limitations on quantized models for accuracy?
[06:14] Priya: There can be small quality changes with aggressive quantization. We'll include model variants in the bench (base fp16, q4/q8 variants) and compare on your eval set. If accuracy drops below your threshold we'll recommend different profile.
[06:27] Kevin: For the pilot gating: if we can't meet SOC2/SSO or data residency, pilot stops. Also if p95 latency > 800ms for our median payloads and accuracy < 85% for the eval set, it's a fail.
[06:42] Alex: Noted. We'll make sure bench targets those metrics; Priya will design bench scenarios.
[06:48] Mark: Network — will we need to open ports inbound for VPC peering?
[06:52] Ethan: For Private VPC we'll ask for peering info; for hosted we'll use outbound connections and can set IP allowlist. We'll send an infra checklist.
[07:02] Sophie: Can you include example audit log schema so our SIEM mapping team can prep?
[07:07] Priya: Yes, we'll share the schema and an example log. It may not be perfect in the first pass — our internal tools sometimes call it 'request_id' as 'req id' in exports — but we'll provide structured JSON.
[07:19] Kevin: Any SLA commitments during pilot? We expect 99.5% availability for our test windows.
[07:25] Alex: For pilot we can commit to a pilot availability target and include runbooks. Production SLAs for Dedicated are in the enterprise contract; we'll include a pilot-level objective in the workbook.
[07:36] (07:37) Priya: Next, bench schedule — we think 2 runs: one baseline with hosted (optimized) and one dedicated/private run if needed. Each run about 2-3 hours plus analysis. We'll need sample datasets and auth creds.
[07:51] Mark: Ok. Sophie will upload the redacted 500-sample eval and a day-in-the-life traffic export (anonymized).
[07:59] Alex: Great. To close: recap of next steps?
[08:03] Sophie: Sophie: we'll provide the samples and volume numbers by next Tuesday.
[08:07] Mark: Mark: I'll provide network constraints and IP ranges.
[08:10] Kevin: Kevin: I'll review the security workbook and confirm KMS constraints.
[08:14] Priya: Priya: I'll send the bench plan and example logs; propose bench date range week of Oct 18.
[08:21] Alex: Alex: I'll send SOC2/ISO certs, security workbook, and SAML metadata.
[08:25] Laura: Thanks, that aligns with our timeline.
[08:28] Alex: Any final Qs?
[08:31] Laura: Not from me, thanks.
[08:33] (08:34) Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-attribution and minor transcription errors (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'SSO' sometimes transcribed as 'S-S-O').
